name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
summary: Former comedian and producer who won the 2019 presidency on an anti-corruption, anti-elite platform and has led Ukraine through the full-scale Russian invasion since 2022. He pursues EU and NATO membership, rejects territorial concessions, and has driven market-oriented and anti-oligarch reforms alongside martial-law restrictions, mobilisation and curbs on Russia-linked parties and a church.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: As president he said in Oct 2019 land should be sold 'for a while' only to Ukrainians, and in a Nov 2019 address that foreigners and part-foreign firms could buy land only if the people consent in an all-Ukrainian referendum; the 2020 law he signed bars foreign buyers and leaves the question to a referendum. Conditional and framed as temporary, hence medium.

corporate-influence.rationale: He submitted the 2021 de-oligarchization bill, which bars officially recognised 'oligarchs' (defined by monopoly, wealth and media influence) from financing parties or taking part in privatisations; it became law in Sept 2021. This restricts rich business money in politics but is aimed at oligarchs, not lobbying by corporations as such.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inaugural address: a country 'where everybody is equal before the law and where the rules of the game are honest and transparent, the same for everyone'; he later drove the anti-oligarch law (barring oligarchs from privatisations). Implied rather than stated about legal privileges for connected firms.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Interview (Jan 2025): says Ukraine is 'ready to open up for investments', wants US and European companies to invest in oil, gas, solar and minerals, and says after the war the country will welcome foreign business; his government relies heavily on foreign aid and loans. He also says he does not want gifts and would rather buy arms with frozen Russian assets.

abortion-legal.rationale: In a 2019 campaign interview, asked about abortion bans such as Poland's, he said abortion should not be banned, that it is a personal choice and that there should be less impingement on human freedom (as reported by Wikipedia; I did not open the original interview), hence medium.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: April 2019 RBC-Ukraine interview: asked about 'sex for money', said it would be possible to 'make a Las Vegas', allowing a designated city or territory to open it up, with taxes paid. A campaign remark; I found no later legislative step, hence low.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Answering a 2022 petition he wrote that 'all people are free and equal in their dignity and rights' and that democracies are measured by equal rights for all citizens; in June 2026 he said all defenders 'have absolutely the same rights'. Inaugural: everyone equal before the law.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Told a heckler in Oct 2019 he would say nothing negative about the LGBT community because Ukraine is an open society ('leave those finally at peace'); in 2022 asked the government to examine civil partnerships; in 2024 said he would sign a civil-partnership law; June 2026: same rights for all. Implies opposition to criminalisation; he did not address criminal law directly.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: June 2026, answering the head of an LGBT veterans' group: 'we are defending the state, we are the same and we have absolutely the same rights, regardless of any prejudices'. Clearly implies LGBT soldiers are equal; he did not name open service.

equal-conscription.rationale: Asked at a press conference about a bill to mobilise women, said he would not sign it ('Women is not [going to be mobilized]') while supporting lowering the men's mobilisation age to 25: conscription for men, not women.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In his 2 March 2022 Babyn Yar address he treated the 1941 massacre as a Holocaust killing site ('you are killing Holocaust victims for the second time') and told the world's Jews 'Nazism is born in silence'; in 2019 he spoke of the Holocaust as a tragedy his people and Israel's lived through.

leader-cult.rationale: Inaugural address: 'I really don't want you to hang my portraits on your office walls. Because a president is not an icon and not an idol. A president is not a portrait.'

recognise-genocide.rationale: Told Netanyahu at a Kyiv briefing: 'I appealed to the Israeli side to recognize the Holodomor as an act of genocide of the Ukrainian people'; at the UN in 2023 he also called Russia's deportation of Ukrainian children 'clearly a genocide'.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inaugural address: to Ukrainians worldwide, 'I will happily provide you with a Ukrainian citizenship. You shouldn't be coming "to visit" Ukraine, you should be coming home.' He offered citizenship rather than speaking of a right.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Introduced the Dec 2022 bill to ban Moscow-affiliated religious organisations, signed the Aug 2024 law (parishes must cut ties with the Russian Orthodox Church within nine months or face court bans), and in July 2025 issued a decree stripping the UOC primate of citizenship. Framed as security against Russian influence, not as a general rule on churches, and contested as a curb on religious freedom.

single-official-language.rationale: Evidence points both ways: he says Ukrainians 'already have a state language - Ukrainian' and rejects Russian as a second official language (2025), but in 2019 said no pressure should be put on the Russian language or on other languages.

conscription.rationale: Declared martial law and ordered general mobilisation on 24 Feb 2022, banned men 18-60 from leaving, said military-age men had a duty to remain, signed the April 2024 mobilisation law lowering the age to 25 and has called for returning draft-age men.

limit-guns.rationale: Mixed: April 2019 he said 'I am against legalization of weapons' in a country at war; May 2026 he called for a 'modern and strong law on civilian firearms' that protects those without weapons and 'realistically regulates' owners, with a bill under preparation.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inaugural address promised soldiers 'worthy and, most importantly, stable financial support' and to create NATO standards; as wartime president has pressed for more funding and arms. He did not speak of police or of more legal authority.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inaugural address: voters 'are tired of the experienced politicians who over the past 28 years created a country of opportunities - opportunities to steal, bribe and loot.' In office he acknowledges corruption exists but says it is being fought, so the 2019 statement is his clearest, and it concerns the previous political class.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Interview: 'I can live by rules, by laws. I believe that this is the only thing that can control any person today. These are the rules and laws of the society or state where you live.' Inaugural: 'everybody is equal before the law'.

proportional-representation.rationale: Asked parliament in his inaugural address to adopt an electoral code with open lists, and in 2019 submitted a bill to elect the Rada by closed-list proportional representation (rejected by parliament). Pursued as a reform, with the choice of list type varying by timing.

direct-votes.rationale: Campaigned on referendums (NATO/EU, land sales to foreigners); in Nov 2019 said a referendum law would 'finally give Ukrainians the right to decide the fate of one or another issue very important for them'; the new referendum law passed in Jan 2021; in 2025 said the people must decide on territory by election or referendum. Supports referendums on big questions, not replacing representatives.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: In March 2022 supported suspending 11 parties with ties to Russia under martial law (the National Security Council decided it). The grounds were security and Russian ties, not a general principle about parties seeking to abolish the constitutional order, and critics call it suppression of opposition.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: At the UN in 2022 demanded a special tribunal for the crime of aggression, repeated it in the Peace Formula, welcomed the ICC arrest warrant for Putin (UNGA 2023) and in May 2023 visited the ICC saying he wants to see Putin tried.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Demands that Russia be held legally accountable for its forces' killings: 'A crime has been committed against Ukraine and we demand just punishment' (2022), 'War crimes must be punished' (2023), and Peace Formula points on prosecution and reparations. Stated about Russia's government and army.

open-diplomacy.rationale: UNGA 2023: peace cannot come from 'dialogue between the so-called great powers somewhere behind the closed doors' but from 'open work of all nations'; 'I am aware of the attempts to make some shady dealings behind the scenes... Let unity decide everything openly.'

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ordered armed resistance to the invasion; his five preconditions for peace include 'determination to defend oneself', and he describes Ukraine's fight as defence of its freedom and life.

non-intervention.rationale: January 2026: called on countries, leaders and international organisations 'to intervene now and help the people' of Iran and hoped they would be freed from the regime.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Points both ways: urged Russians not to submit to Russia's 'criminal mobilisation' (2022), but runs a mobilisation, criminalises desertion and calls for returning draft-age men in Ukraine.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: UNGA 2025: 'If a nation wants peace, it still has to work on weapons. It's sick - but that's the reality'; also 'weapons decide who survives'.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Seeks NATO membership ('invitation to NATO' is point one of his 2024 Victory Plan; says security guarantees without the US are impossible). He did say in March 2022 he would discuss neutrality in return for guarantees, but his latest position is to join NATO.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Describes NATO as 'a very good alliance', 'defensive' and 'protection', and wants Ukraine in it with US-backed guarantees; he does not address bringing troops home but opposes ending alliances.

collective-defense.rationale: Interview: NATO countries 'don't fight. There is no war on the land of any of these NATO countries... it works'; wants NATO membership and US-backed guarantees for Ukraine, and says without the United States there would be no NATO.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Signed Ukraine's EU membership application four days into the invasion and says 'our people have chosen Europe'; wants Ukraine to be an equal member. Does not speak of pooling sovereignty by name.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Jan 2026: says British and French military presence in Ukraine after a ceasefire is 'mandatory' for security guarantees. He speaks of foreign troops, not bases by name.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Oct 2024: said Ukraine would have 'either nuclear weapons... or some kind of alliance' and chooses NATO; clarified 'We are not asking for nuclear weapons to be given or returned... we need NATO'. Prefers an ally's protection.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: 2019: ready for peace 'without giving up our territories - ever'. 2025-26: refuses to withdraw from Donbas ('I will never leave Donbass'), says swaps are not in Ukraine's interest, though he accepted freezing the front line and says the people would decide by referendum.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inaugural: 'Our next challenge is to return the lost territories... Both Crimea and Donbas are Ukrainian lands'; Peace Formula and UNGA 2022 demand restoration of the internationally recognised border.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: UNGA 2022: denounced 'pseudo-referendums in the occupied territories' and demanded 'punishment for violation of borders' until the internationally recognised border is restored; signed the Crimea de-occupation strategy (2021).

national-self-determination.rationale: UNGA 2023: aggression against any state should end 'not because your land will be divided' but because 'your territory and sovereignty will be fully restored'; supports each nation's sovereignty and says Ukrainians 'have chosen Europe'.

refugee-return.rationale: UNGA 2023: 'Deported people must come back home' and Russia must return the Ukrainian children it deported; the Peace Formula includes release and return of deportees. Applied to Ukrainians; descendants not addressed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Feb 2025 evening address: 'we are preparing to launch four more reactors' at Khmelnytskyi (two VVER-1000 and two Westinghouse AP1000) to avoid electricity imports and give cheaper power.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: COP26 (2021): Ukraine aims to cut greenhouse gas emissions 65% by 2030 and reach climate neutrality not later than 2060; UNGA 2023 said humanity is failing on its climate objectives. Did not call for 'drastic' action.

online-participation.rationale: Interview: for wartime elections 'we need to think about' changing the system, including online voting, despite cyber-attack fears; also stresses digital government via Diia. Open to it rather than committed.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inaugural address: 'Ukrainian is not what's written in your passport. Ukrainian is what's right here'; Ukrainian- and Russian-speaking people are all Ukrainians, and he rejects Russia's claim that Russian speakers belong with Russia.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He announces successive statutory increases, from 5,000 to 6,500 hryvnias.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He calls the state an inefficient manager and favors private investment.

public-ownership.rationale: He promotes energy privatization while retaining strategic assets and imposing wartime state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He endorses higher resource-use payments from oligarchs to finance children’s accounts.

property-fundamental.rationale: He personally orders strategic assets expropriated for wartime management.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Industrial-pollution controls coexist with his later demand for deregulation and reduced state pressure.

cut-welfare.rationale: He defends continuing pension indexation and necessary social payments during war.

more-religion-public.rationale: His 2026 address advocates unity of state, churches, military and society.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He directs a programme protecting heritage and expanding Ukrainian cultural production.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He demands UN reform so security institutions can decide and influence events.

revolution-justified.rationale: He celebrates the two Maidan revolutions as struggles for freedom and democracy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His plan directs domestic and allied investment into defense production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He limits farmland concentration and promotes access to individual homeownership.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Asked his ideology, he identifies ending war and improving economic outcomes.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He affirms Israel’s right to self-defense alongside Palestinian statehood.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He explicitly combines museum preservation with contemporary-art development.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He assigns government active roles in healthcare, pensions and education.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He describes the presidency as employment by citizens for a fixed term.

separated-powers.rationale: Judicial independence claims coexist with the 2025 curtailment and restoration of anticorruption independence.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He urges solidarity regardless of language, religion, gender or age.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He maintains martial-law restrictions, including postponed elections and restricted political activity.

party-controls-media.rationale: He consolidates television news under state wartime coordination.

ban-cartels.rationale: He demands effective antitrust tools against oligarchic control of entire sectors.

religious-nation.rationale: He bases national solidarity on people of different religions, rather than religious uniformity.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He suspends Russia-linked opposition parties during martial law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He wants citizens repeatedly influencing national and regional decisions.

social-market-economy.rationale: His plan combines entrepreneurial freedom with social payments and public support.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He traces Ukrainian identity through the Lavra and the millennium of Kyivan Rus’.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He frames legitimate military purpose as protection against aggression, not attacks on neighbors.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He describes ongoing Russian plans to seize additional Ukrainian regions and cities.

arms-reduction.rationale: He calls for slowing the global weapons race while building necessary defenses.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: He says natural resources belong to every citizen and charges users for children’s benefit.

notes:
Positions are his own words or record as president (since 2019), mostly via English reports of speeches and interviews because president.gov.ua refused automated access. Stances that changed: in March 2022 he said he would discuss neutrality for security guarantees, but he now seeks NATO membership; in 2019 he wanted open-list proportional elections; on guns he opposed legalisation in 2019 but backs a regulated civilian-firearms law in 2026. The 2025 NABU/SAPO law (signed 22 July, reversed 31 July after protests) was not used because he did not state a position matching any statement. Left null (no evidence of his own position): same-sex marriage (he cited the constitution and backs civil partnerships), death penalty, tax rates, welfare, healthcare, unions, abortion limits beyond his 2019 remark.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 32 answers taken from it, 27 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass with no previous answers consulted; living subject, no inferred answers. One of ten priority statements answered. Direct endorsement of Maidan supports justified revolution; it does not establish Marxist class theory, vanguardism or abolition of wages. Profit from investment is not automatically an answer about necessary worker exploitation. Full remaining statements reviewed. Strategic ownership is mixed with privatization, and regulation combines environmental controls with later deregulation. Natural-resource dividends are a child-account proposal, not a universal adult basic income. Pension support does not settle private pension accounts. Healthcare financing was checked in health.txt; ministers’ proposals and critics’ accounts are not attributed as his universal-coverage position. The RBC interview was read in full in Ukrainian; abortion and geographically qualified sex-work answers are his, whereas medical cannabis does not answer all-drug legalization. Civil partnerships and equal LGBT dignity do not settle same-sex marriage or every gender-identity law. The Constitution Day speech supports a public church role but does not clearly answer strict legal church–state separation or divine political authority. Protection of church heritage does not establish legal precedence for a national denomination. Museum and cultural support is not a doctrine of sacred nationhood or literal canonization of fallen soldiers. Minority protection rhetoric does not by itself settle institutional autonomy. Personal attendance at prayer was not used as evidence. The 2025 institutional reversal is recorded as mixed, not silently replaced by earlier independence rhetoric. Wartime restrictions are assigned from his actions despite democratic language. UN institutional reform is supported through his criticism of ineffective vetoes, but permissionless foreign force is not inferred from it. Peaceful demonstrations abroad and concern for Iran do not establish support for arming insurgents. His AI partnership and September 2026 warning about autonomous battlefield decisions were checked in full; neither establishes algorithmic civil government, generalized acceleration regardless of disruption, or a literal human-extinction priority. The independent environmental working group’s framework was read but is not automatically attributed to him. Climate concern and forestry projects do not prove intrinsic nature rights, natural-capital accounting or the exact intergenerational Earth-undamaged proposition. No quiz-site estimates used.
